title: Valon lands $150M series D to grow AI-native ValonOS
key_facts: Valon Technologies raised $150 million in a Series D round at a $2.3 billion valuation, announced on Monday 5 Oct 2026, to accelerate adoption of its AI-native ValonOS servicing platform (HousingWire).
The round doubles its prior valuation; new investor Ribbit Capital joins existing backer Andreessen Horowitz and other prior investors.
The money will go to product development and hiring in engineering, product, deployment and go-to-market roles based in New York and San Francisco, plus remote positions.
Valon says it has more than $200 million in contracted annual recurring revenue for ValonOS and is under contract to power servicing for roughly one in six outstanding US mortgages.

Carrington Mortgage Services completed its acquisition of Valon Mortgage two months ago (announced in May), adding about 810,000 loans; Carrington adopted ValonOS as its core servicing platform, joining ServiceMac, and Newrez is also a client.

ValonOS consolidates loan data, investor reporting, workflows, compliance logic and money movement in one system of record; AI agents can handle tasks such as answering homeowner emails, allocating payments and running escrow analyses.
CEO Andrew Wang says mortgage servicing has run on aging mainframe systems for sixty years, which is the company's own view.
